paper.title_en: Beyond the Diffusion Coefficient: Propagators and Memory in Cosmic Ray Transport
paper.abstract_en: Cosmic ray (CR) transport is usually modeled with a single diffusion coefficient, but this description captures only the growth of the variance. Distinct transport mechanisms can share the same effective diffusion coefficient while producing different particle distributions and approaches to the diffusive limit. The distinction matters in multiphase, structured and time-dependent media, and is reflected in the observed variation of CR transport near pulsar wind nebulae, supernova remnants and molecular clouds, and in particle-tracing studies that show both superdiffusion and subdiffusion. We therefore develop a propagator-based framework centered on the probability distribution of particle positions, or equivalently its Fourier-Laplace transform. This object is compact and complete for the observable spatial transport. It naturally reveals if large scale transport has memory: when the CR flux depends on earlier rather than just the instantaneous pressure gradient. Such memory arises when dynamically relevant transport states, such as trapping or phase changes, are not retained in the macroscopic description. Using the Montroll-Weiss formalism, we measure the propagator directly from trajectories, recover the associated memory kernel, and represent broad kernels with a Prony expansion. Applied to a multiphase medium, the framework shows that slow regions can regulate escape without dominating the total residence time budget. We also introduce an accelerated Monte Carlo method for coarse-grained transport, showing that if trapping structures evolve while particles are still sampling them, the static long-time limit need not be reached. This provides a foundation for observational applications, particle-tracing measurements and CR-MHD closures.
